l.i: & absolutum, tamen non per se immediate im-

main_text.l: ut illa divina voluntas impleatur. Sed Resp. 1.
Iesuita falsum & Dei perfectione indignum
praesupponit, nempe Dei decretum absolutum,
quo voluntas Physice praedeterminatur, ex-
trahere ipsam a naturali agendi modo, hoc-
cine nos docemus? Evince si potes argumen-
to, & Deum non posse indeclinabiliter, &
tamen modo connaturalissimo[?] voluntatem
flectere Deo imperfectionem aspergit, &
dominium in actus liberos non mediocriter la-
befactar. 2 Praedeterminatio Physica etiam
ponit medium morale aptissimum, quippe vo-
luntas est agens vere ethicum & morale, etiam
Dei determinatione, & propter moralem sua-
sionem

page.notes: Fragment at the head of the page ("rorum") is cut off; the first letter is doubtful and marked [?]. "connaturalissimo" is doubtful: the printed letters after "connatural" are run together, so the ending is marked [?]. The word "sua-sionem" is broken across the line with a printed hyphen and read as "suasionem". Italic runs follow the printed type; "(inquit)" is roman. Long s is rendered as s throughout. Stray marks at the bottom right and left edges are not printed text and are omitted.
